- **invariant** `blocks/step-structural-edits-machine-aware-they`: Step-structural edits - `addStep`, `deleteStep`, `duplicateStep`, `setLayerActivation`, `renameStep` - are MACHINE-AWARE: they move the bound waypoint with the step and CARRY the walk's arrows across the change, and they are the ONLY way waypoints are added or removed. `reconnectPath` mints a plain `next` only for genuinely new pairs, and `syncWaypointNames` syncs names one way.

- **rule** `blocks/copies-keyframes-but-never-lands-after`: `duplicateStep` copies keyframes but NOT `reveals` or `hides` and never lands after Out; `deleteStep` returns the layers it revealed to appearing with Play under the channel's default motion; `addStep` makes an empty content step just before Out, or at an explicit index clamped between the entrance and Out. `setLayerActivation` carries a layer's tuned reveal keyframes when it moves between presses and writes the channel's default motion when it enters or leaves the press world, emptied presses disappearing and default step names renumbering.
- **rule** `blocks/css-property-holding-list-functions-data`: `filter` is ONE CSS property holding a LIST of functions, so the data keeps ONE `filter` track of composed strings like `blur(8px) brightness(1.6)`; `filterTrack.ts` parses and composes that string so each function in `FILTER_FUNCS` - blur, brightness, saturate, hueRotate, and glow as a colourless centred drop-shadow - can be its own Inspector row.
- **rule** `blocks/delete-nothing-can-reach-never-repair`: Delete a `BuildingBlock` nothing can reach; never repair one, and never add a second implementation of playout logic beside an existing one. Reachability is whatever `src/ai/stubProvider.ts` actually passes to `block(...)`, so read that file before calling an entry dead.
- **rule** `blocks/deliberately-creates-pose-off-hold-legitimate`: `addState` deliberately creates a POSE - Off and a hold are legitimate states - and attaching content is an explicit act through `setStateTimeline`, which gives an off-path state its own inline timeline or takes it away. `addState`/`deleteState` are OFF-PATH only and the initial state never goes; `addGroup`/`removeGroup` never remove main; `setStatePosition` writes the additive `at` field.

- **rule** `blocks/emits-positioned-commented-css-rule-shared`: `insertLottieElement` emits a positioned `<div id="lottie-*" data-gfx data-lottie="<path>">`, a commented CSS rule, and ONE shared idempotent bootstrap in the JS that decodes an inlined `data:` URL with `atob` rather than fetching it, so `file://` playout works. - **rule** `blocks/gate-code-never-category-standard-contract`: Gate `addCatalogLine` on the CODE, never the category: the standard contract's `{p}-mask` plus `{p}-name|-title|-extra` line idiom, cloned from the last of the HOST's lines (`detectPrefix` filters out an inserted graphic's namespaced lines), classed by the assembler's `lineClassFor` ladder and falling back to the last line's class when the design ships no rule for the canonical one. Anything off-shape returns null.
- **rule** `blocks/honest-gate-code-derived-never-category`: `insertBlocker` is the honest gate and it is code-derived, never a category list: a donor with no editable animation data block, donor step `calls`/`dynamics`, or functions in the donor JS beyond the standard scaffold each refuse the insert WITH the reason.
- **rule** `blocks/image-twin-mask-registry-part-sized`: `addPlacedImageSlot` is the image twin of `addPlacedLine`: an `<img id="fN">` in the mask as a registry `image` part, a sized slot box with a dashed empty-slot mark keyed on `.has-image` that `setFieldValue` already toggles, and a filelist DataField; `slotSize`/`setSlotSize` are the corner handle's resize pair. Both adds are gated by `designBoxInfo` - a box whose unit carries `<prefix>-art` - and return null off-shape.
- **rule** `blocks/keep-donor-middle-steps-rather-than`: Keep the donor's MIDDLE steps rather than flattening them: each becomes its own host default-path step through the machine-aware `addStep(data, at)`, inserted CONTIGUOUSLY after wherever the run starts, with `reveals` and `hides` carried through the same namespace rewrite as every other selector and every keyframe time speed-normalized onto the host's base. `buildDonor(variant, steps)` is the ONE donor build.
- **rule** `blocks/keyframe-where-number-string-filter-clippath`: A keyframe is `{ time, value, ease? }` where `value` is a number or a STRING - filter and clipPath interpolate as strings - and `ease` is the ease INTO the keyframe, defaulting to the step's.
- **rule** `blocks/legacy-region-reader-nothing-more-reads`: `timelineModel.ts` is the legacy-region READER and nothing more: `parseTimeline` reads a region and `buildOverview` builds the cue-segmented overview. The literal patchers that used to live beside them went with Phase 8, and a legacy region is now read-only.
- **rule** `blocks/per-direction-delay-hold-before-motion`: A per-direction DELAY is a hold before the motion: the written keyframes shift later within the step, the step grows by the hold, and step-level `calls` and `dynamics` shift with it.
- **rule** `blocks/per-track-loop-gsap-values-repeat`: `loops` is `loops[selector][prop] = { repeat, yoyo?, repeatDelay? }`, a PER-TRACK loop in GSAP's values (repeat -1 forever, yoyo breathing back and forth) that the interpreter plays in its own repeating sub-timeline, so an ambient breath lives in the same data as every other track and the `layers` arrays are untouched.
- **rule** `blocks/picker-draws-six-cards-ten-slide`: The picker draws SIX cards, not ten (`MOTION_FAMILIES`): Slide's four members and Wipe's two are one motion with a DIRECTION and render as arrows in the cell. The bank keeps all ten `MotionPresetId`s - every arrow picks a real one and a saved graphic names one.
- **rule** `blocks/position-inserted-element-lower-left-action`: Position an inserted element with `positionForNewElement` in the lower-left action-safe area, tag it `data-gfx` and style it with `textCssRule`. A block groups under a hierarchical `path` and names the `primaryTab` to reveal after applying. Animation blocks come in two tracks: CSS (`@keyframes` plus a class on the element) and GSAP (a tween injected into `play()`/`stop()`).
- **rule** `blocks/pure-transform-emitting-mask-wrapper-plus`: `addPlacedLine` is ONE pure transform emitting the mask wrapper plus span, the placement and type rules in the assembler's exact idiom, and the SPX DataField - no JS change, because `update()` binds by id. The element lands after the unit's last mask or the artwork's END, after `</svg>` for an inlined SVG and never inside it; new lines stack under the lowest existing line, inherit its look, and default to `shrink` with the room to the artwork's right edge.
- **rule** `blocks/read-write-placed-line-whole-look`: `lineTextStyle`/`setLineTextStyle` read and write a placed line's whole LOOK on the span's `#fN` rule - font-family (a bundled font id, the design font, or 'custom' when hand-written; picking a bundled face also ships its `@font-face`, deduped by the emitted rule), font-size, weight, color, line-height, letter-spacing - plus the anchor as the wrapper's `translateX` shift on `#fwN`. Every write is a `setCssDeclaration` patch in the rule's own idiom, so the canvas gestures and these controls stay one language.
- **rule** `blocks/reads-hooks-their-resolved-positions-importer`: `parseTimeline` reads `tl.call(fn)` hooks with their resolved positions and the importer attaches them to the enter or out step as speed-relative `calls`, which is what lets game timers flip to data blocks; it also reads a repeating tween's `repeat`/`yoyo`/`repeatDelay` and writes a step loop when the tween's values are finite LITERALS. Neither calls nor dynamics shift a tween's INDEX, so the legacy patchers are untouched.
- **rule** `blocks/reads-lit-card-back-data-times`: `currentMotionPreset(template, data, phase)` READS the lit card back from the data - times and values per target, ease ignored, because an easing is a modifier and not another motion. Nothing is stamped into the block for it, so a hand-edited timeline honestly lights nothing.
- **rule** `blocks/returns-semantic-errors-warnings-while-shape`: `validateMachine` returns the semantic errors and warnings for `validateTemplate` while the SHAPE gate stays in animData's `isAnimData`, and `stateProblems` returns the subset belonging to ONE state - unreachable, or a timer on a timeline that never ends - STRUCTURALLY as `{groupId, stateId, severity, message}` so the node editor can mark the box it is about. `validateMachine` folds them back into its own lists.
- **rule** `blocks/rewrites-asset-path-exact-string-replace`: `moveAsset` rewrites an asset path with an EXACT-STRING replace across html, css and js - the verbatim-path convention `inlineAssetRefs` relies on - and a `./`-prefixed reference is covered because the bare path is a substring. Anything cleverer breaks the preview's inlining.
- **rule** `blocks/scope-all-whole-graphic-adopting-donor`: Scope 'all' is the whole graphic adopting the donor's full choreography plus the chosen or donor step duration and ease, SKIPPING press-revealed layers whose entrance belongs to their press; it also swaps the target phase's step `calls` and `dynamics` for the donor's, both scaled to the settled duration. Per-layer applies never touch `calls` or `dynamics` - those are step-level, not layer motion.
- **rule** `blocks/spec-action-what-operator-may-right`: `operatorEvents(group, stateId)` is the spec's Action - what an operator may do RIGHT NOW - and it IS the structural guard; `allOperatorEvents` is the whole machine's set and `timerTransition` the timer edge. `machineControls` is THE one button-list merge every control surface renders, dressing declared `machine.controls` entries over the authored events, and it SKIPS an undeclared `next` because the lifecycle button already fires it.
- **rule** `blocks/steps-clips-preserve-mode-keeps-keyframe`: Steps are CLIPS: `resizeStep` in 'preserve' mode keeps keyframe timing - extending leaves settled air, shrinking clamps at the last keyframe so motion never silently truncates - and 'stretch' (Alt) scales times proportionally. `setLayerHide` is the early-exit twin, writing or clearing a step's `hides` for a layer, clamped after its activation and cleared when hiding at Out, driven by the timeline block's RIGHT edge.
- **rule** `blocks/strings-interpolate-too-both-keyframes-have`: STRINGS interpolate too when both keyframes have the same shape - the numbers inside them lerp in place, which is what GSAP does at runtime - so the Inspector tracks the preview instead of stepping, and it is written generically so clipPath mask-wipes benefit identically. Differently-shaped strings hold the previous keyframe; a step without the track inherits the last keyframe value from an earlier step; null means the layer's design CSS state. A LOOPING track folds the query time back into one pass through `loopedTime`.
- **rule** `blocks/takes-easing-resolved-gsap-pair-stamped`: `applyPresetData` takes an easing resolved to a GSAP pair and stamped onto the written keyframes so it never disturbs a shared step, plus an optional per-direction duration that sets the target step's length and scales the donor keyframes to fit. 'in' is layer-relative and targets the step where THAT layer becomes active, 'out' always targets the final step, and 'both' writes both, independently editable after.
- **rule** `blocks/time-legacy-converter-parses-legacy-marked`: `importAnimData` is the ONE-TIME legacy converter: it parses a legacy marked region through timelineModel's `parseTimeline` and converts the choreography into `AnimData`, taking a `to()`'s from-values from the settled `DESIGN_STATE` table. It serves read-only rendering of legacy templates on the new timeline AND the explicit, undoable convert-on-first-motion-edit; a template the old parser cannot read stays hand-crafted.
- **rule** `blocks/way-emit-preset-region-template-structure`: `emitPresetRegion(template, presetId, opts?)` is the ONE way to emit a preset's region for a template, with the structure facts read off its HTML, and `presetsForType`/`anyPresetById` are the one lookup for every category's presets. Three callers share that one shape: `presetApply` derives a preset's keyframes by emitting a region and converting it through the importer, `LegacyTimeline`'s start-over writes it converted over an unconvertible region, and `ai/claudeProvider.ts`'s `exampleWithAuthoringRegion` emits it into the model's worked example.
- **rule** `blocks/what-moves-root-direct-element-children`: `motionTargets` is WHAT MOVES: the root's direct element children that are DRAWN - hidden `.noacg-data-source` holders, script, style and form sources and inline-hidden elements are skipped - read off the HTML every time and each addressed by the most readable UNIQUE selector, an id, else a class no other element carries, else `root > :nth-child(n)`. The root itself never takes a track, because the interpreter owns its opacity.
- **rule** `blocks/writes-datafield-element-static-text-markup`: `setFieldDefault` writes the DataField `value` AND the element's static text in the markup, so the pre-play preview and the hidden-source categories stay in sync; `setFieldTitle` changes only the operator-facing label and the layer metadata, never the element id - every binding, rule and keyframe track hangs off that id.
